title: Representative Training Notes: Quantity per 30 Days on Continuous Glucose Monitoring Supply Program Renewal Orders
content:
Prescribers do not all write the quantity on a renewal order for the CGM supply allowance (HCPCS A4239) the same way. Under the Continuous Glucose Monitoring Supply Program, the units per 30 days counted on the grant written from a renewal order are read by the following rule.

> **Rule.** The quantity-reading adjustment replaces the order's units per 30 days by the convention the prescriber used: when the order states exactly the tier's allowance per 30 days times the 30-day blocks of one standard shipment, it is a per-shipment count and the units per 30 days are that quantity divided by those blocks; when it states any other quantity above the tier's allowance per 30 days, the quantity cannot be read and the grant carries no units until the prescriber corrects the order; otherwise the order's quantity as written applies.

**Q. Which quantity is read?** The quantity per 30 days stated on the renewal, the newest written order of the CGM supply allowance on the program.

**Q. What is the tier's allowance per 30 days?** The tier's sensor allowance units per 30 days of supply.

**Q. What is "the 30-day blocks of one standard shipment"?** The tier's standard days of supply per refill shipment divided by 30. The per-shipment figure is the tier's sensor allowance units per 30 days of supply multiplied by that number of blocks.

**Q. What are the figures on each tier?**

| Tier | Sensor allowance units per 30 days | Standard days of supply per refill shipment | 30-day blocks in one shipment | Per-shipment figure |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| CGM Self-Pay Program | 1 | 30 | 1 | 1 |
| CGM Commercial HMO Program | 1 | 30 | 1 | 1 |
| CGM Commercial PPO Program | 1 | 90 | 3 | 3 |
| CGM Medicare Advantage Program | 1 | 90 | 3 | 3 |
| CGM Original Medicare Program | 1 | 90 | 3 | 3 |
| CGM Medicaid Program | 1 | 30 | 1 | 1 |

**Q. How does each stated quantity read on the CGM Original Medicare Program?** There the allowance is 1 unit per 30 days and one standard shipment is 3 blocks, so the per-shipment figure is 3.

| Quantity per 30 days stated on the order | How it reads | Units per 30 days |
|---|---|---|
| 0 or 1 (not above the allowance of 1) | as written | the order's quantity as written |
| 2 (above 1, not 3) | cannot be read | none; the grant carries no units until the prescriber corrects the order |
| 3 (exactly the per-shipment figure) | per-shipment count | 3 divided by 3, that is 1 |
| 4 or more (above 1, not 3) | cannot be read | none; the grant carries no units until the prescriber corrects the order |

**Q. What about a tier whose standard shipment is a single 30-day block?** There the per-shipment figure equals the allowance of 1: a quantity of 1 reads either as a per-shipment count of 1 divided by 1 or as written, giving 1 unit per 30 days in both readings, and any quantity above 1 cannot be read.
